summary: Weekly POC sync to review benchmark results comparing Redwood inference runs to the customer's baseline provider. Redwood shows better median latency and higher throughput at target tail latency for our recommended batching/cache configuration; some parity/variance in 99th percentile under heavy multi-tenant load. Discussed tuning (batch sizes, KV cache hit rates, quantization tradeoffs) and next steps to reproduce a handful of baseline edge cases.
transcript: Header: Date: 2025-02-19 15:00 UTC | Duration: 45m | Location: Zoom
Attendees: Jordan Lee (Redwood AE), Samir Patel (Redwood SE), Maria Gomez (StratosAI CTO), Rajesh Patel (Eng Lead), Tina Chen (ML Engineer)
[00:00] Jordan: Hey everyone, thanks for hopping on. Quick agenda — benchmark review, tuning notes, next steps. We'll try to keep to 45 minutes.
[00:22] Maria: Thanks Jordan, yeah we got the notes, excited to see the numbers. We've been running the BaselineProvider workloads for the last week so should be a good compare.
[00:35] Samir: cool, i have the slides pulled up. just a heads up some of the metric names in our export got munged by the exporter so you'll see e.g., 'P90' as p9 sometimes, small things.
[00:50] Raj: that's fine. main things we care about: median latency under 512 tokens, tail at 99 under load, and sustained throughput for our 200-rps mix.
[01:10] Jordan: perfect. Samir, can you walk through the median numbers first?

[01:18] Samir: yeah, so slide 3. median latency for the Redwood Dedicate run — i'll keep saying Dedicate, our bad, Redwood Dedicated — was 42 ms for 512 token average requests. BaselineProvider median was 78 ms under the same request mix.
[01:45] Tina: that delta is... pretty big. were these runs single-tenant or multi-tenant?
[01:52] Samir: single-tenant reserved pool with autoscale off for parity. We then did a multi-tenant run later to test tail behavior.
[02:05] Maria: what about throughput numbers? we need to hit 200 rps at p95 < 200 ms ideally.
[02:12] Samir: slide 5 — throughput: Redwood sustained 260 rps with p95 at 110 ms and p99 at 230 ms. BaselineProvider sustained 190 rps at p95 180 ms and p99 420 ms.
[02:35] Jordan: so for your SLA target 200 rps/p95<200, both can meet p95 but Redwood gives more headroom and much better p99.
[02:50] Raj: interesting. can you share what batching config you used? our ops team needs the exact flags.

[02:57] Samir: yes, we used dynamic batching with max batch size 32, target latency ceiling 120 ms, and continuous KV cache warmup. quantization: int8 with per-channel symmetric — that last bit matters for throughput.
[03:25] Tina: int8 gave you no quality regressions? we saw some token shift on named entities in a few tests last week.

[03:34] Samir: good call. we ran evals on your golden prompt set; overall Rouge/L2 metrics held within your 0.5% tolerance except for a few entity-heavy prompts. we can toggle mixed-precision for those routes or pin to float16.
[03:55] Maria: that's acceptable as long as we can route specific endpoints to higher-precision models. what's the KV cache hit rate you observed?

[03:63] Samir: (laughs) 03:63 — exporter glitch — KV cache hit was ~68% on average for the conversational workload; after we added prefix caching for common templates it went up to 82% and latencies dropped about 18%.
[04:20] Jordan: important note — the baseline runs did not use prefix caching in their default config, which explains some of the gap.
[04:32] Raj: on tail latency — you mentioned p99 was still higher under multi-tenant load?

[04:38] Samir: yes. in the multi-tenant stress run where we injected noisy neighbors at 60% of the cluster, Redwood p99 moved from 230 ms to ~520 ms, whereas BaselineProvider jumped to ~900 ms. We have fallbacks to smaller model variants and region routing to keep critical endpoints under SLO.
[05:05] Tina: can you reproduce the noisy neighbor pattern on our infra? we want to see exact failure mode for our traffic shape.
[05:12] Jordan: absolutely, that's one of the next steps. Samir will detail the traffic profile he used.
[05:20] Samir: profile: 70/20/10 read/write-ish mix, 30% long-context (1-2k tokens). injected 60% extra synthetic requests to simulate other teams. I'll paste the JMeter config in the spreadsheet.
[05:45] Maria: did you also test private deployment shapes? our security folks care about V P C and KMS behavior, and we have a separate on-prem bucket.
[05:54] Samir: yes, we ran a Redwood Private emulation in a VPC and validated KMS integration — keywrap latency adds about 8-12 ms but everything stayed within p95 for the 200 rps case.
[06:12] Raj: the baseline we ran had a different quantization stack — can you confirm that the BaselineProvider numbers are their default managed endpoint config?

[06:20] Jordan: yes we asked StratosAI to export their BaselineProvider runs and we used what they gave us. there may be small differences but we tried to align as much as possible — same model family, same prompt mix.
[06:35] Maria: any anomalies in tokenization or prompt truncation between runs? we noticed a couple of truncated outputs before.

[06:44] Samir: good point. we saw a few truncation incidents on BaselineProvider when context approached 2k; Redwood's continuous KV cache preserved state better so truncations were less frequent. I'll flag specific log lines in the spreadsheet.
[07:02] Tina: regarding cost: rough per-token cost comparison? we need ballpark numbers to present to finance.

[07:09] Jordan: top-line: under our optimized config Redwood's per-1000-token cost is about 18% lower than BaselineProvider, mostly due to batching and higher cache hit rates. we'll include a detailed cost breakdown in the file.
[07:28] Raj: question on the 99th spikes — do you think kernel selection could be tuned further? You mentioned compilation/kernels earlier.

[07:36] Samir: yes, kernel selection matters. we picked optimized kernels for long-seq attention and used the newer sparse attention kernel on some runs. I can share exact flags; some of these are experimental but stable enough for pilot.
[07:52] Maria: okay, what are the suggested mitigations we can test next week to tighten p99?

[07:58] Samir: three quick ones: 1) smaller max batch for latency-sensitive routes, 2) increase prefix cache and pre-warm for known templates, 3) enable region+variant fallback for tail cases. Also consider pinned reserved capacity for critical endpoints.
[08:17] Tina: can you quantify the tradeoff if we reduce max batch from 32 to 16? what's the throughput hit?
[08:24] Samir: roughly you lose about 12-16% throughput but median latency improves by 20-25% and p99 drops by ~18% in our tests. exact depends on request mix.
[08:40] Jordan: I'll note that as a recommended route: use smaller batch for user-interactive endpoints and keep larger batch sizes for background bulk generation.
[08:52] Raj: one operational ask — can you provide the exact CPU/GPU and memory utilization graphs aligned with the runs? our infra team will want those.
[08:59] Samir: yes, we'll attach GPU util, host CPU, and memory traces in the CSV export. also raw profiler traces for the slow samples.
[09:12] Maria: any security blockers surfaced during the POC?
[09:17] Jordan: none new. we provided SOC 2 docs, SAML/SSO integration guide, and KMS flow. StratosAI's security team asked a few follow-ups but nothing blocking the pilot.
[09:30] Tina: okay good. last bit — we have a few golden prompts that failed generation quality under int8, i'll share those as examples. we may want mixed precision for those routes.
[09:40] Samir: agreed. we'll propose per-route precision policies in the follow-up doc.

[09:46] Jordan: let's recap next steps quickly — Samir to share exact serving config and kernel flags; Jordan to send updated benchmark CSV and cost breakdown; Tina to run extra 2k tests; we'll reconvene early next week.
[10:01] Maria: sounds good. can we get the spreadsheet by Friday so our finance/security teams can review?
[10:07] Jordan: yes — Friday EOD. that's 2025-02-21 for clarity.
[10:15] Raj: one more tiny thing — competitor note: BaselineProvider says they can do better in region X if you use their managed autoscale; curious if Redwood measured cross-region variance.
[10:26] Samir: we ran region parity tests — variance was minimal in NA regions, slightly higher in APAC due to infra cold starts. we'll include region breakdown.
[10:40] Tina: thanks, that's helpful. no other questions from me.
[10:46] Maria: same here. thanks everybody for the thorough run. looking forward to the CSV and configs.
[10:53] Jordan: thanks all. action items and next steps will be in the follow-up email. we'll set the next sync for Monday if that works.
[11:02] Raj: Monday works. bye all.
[11:05] (call ends)
